changes.title: Reserve administrative authoring and report missing source-protection declarations
changes.summary: Breaking: ia author now refuses workspace, agent, mandate, system, schema, agent-profile and hook mutations for every actor, including an ungoverned one. The boundary covers new records, field edits and relationship edits and prevents indirect changes to participant rights, admission, workspace closure and host edit guards; it also refuses benign edits to these words. Existing profile, ownership and binding-mandate refusals keep precedence, previews remain read-only, and owner source edits followed by validation remain the administrative path. ia doctor reports a read-only source-protection warning when restrictive authored mandates have no supported full-tree .ia/src hook declaration for all edit tools. Declaration evidence is not host enforcement; no hook path is widened, no starter is written, and the current guard still checks Synthesis rather than word exclusions on file bytes. No stored-data migration is required. These are cooperative CLI boundaries, not authentication or filesystem isolation.

changes.title: An authored revision that runtime-band sources do not move: body(K), the packet, the host note and retention read it
changes.summary: @inventarch/graph exports authoredRevisionOf(registry, inputs, derived?) beside revisionOf: the same SHA-256 over the same inputs without the sources at runtime placement (band 0), each runtime-placed input whose path derived names (a derived revision-only input no record compiles from) kept, and the registry, language version and kernel digest hashed as revisionOf hashes them; with no other source at runtime placement it equals revisionOf, and load and Graph.revision are unchanged. @inventarch/db readers and handles add authoredRevision (the root view's), previousAuthoredRevision and capturedAuthoredRevision, and Snapshot adds authoredRevision (the read view's); each keeps the .ia/.db-inputs.json input and the view registry, so a folder, floor-origin, authored-root or activation change still moves it, as does a source at runtime placement that adds a system folder or declares a `@system` or `@schema`, and with no source at runtime placement it equals revision, so a workspace with none keeps every revision and digest it had. revision keeps its meaning for scopes, revision read bindings (IA-DB-STALE), draft previews and the cache. Retention now keys on the authored revision: the previous snapshot is the most recent one whose authored revision differs, so a change to runtime-band sources alone rotates nothing, in a handle, in a new handle or in the capture pair writeCapture and planCapture keep; and a capture is trusted by its authored revision and the identity, band and digest of the membership rows of its records not at runtime placement, so one that differs from the fresh snapshot only in runtime-band rows, or in the roots a runtime-band `@workspace` declares, stays current. ia-snapshot-1 documents gain an optional authoredRevision key, which @inventarch/cli's ia capture now writes; a document without it names its revision as its authored revision, a malformed one is no capture, the format name is unchanged, and ia capture --json keeps its keys while its text now says the previous capture moved or was kept because the authored revision changed or did not; ia position's freshness line now names the capture's revision as its authored revision. Breaking: @inventarch/runtime's body(K) revision (the format keeps its name, ia.position-body.v1), the position packet's revision and provenance revision, renderHost's ia-generated line, the consumer skill's Source revision and the receipt's revision, the delivery view's revision, and the host note's revision, capturedRevision and previousRevision, and so its freshness, are now authored revisions, so a source at runtime placement that adds no system folder and declares no `@system` or `@schema` moves none of them while handle.revision moves; executeOwned takes the authored revision as its base, refusing with IA-EXEC-SOURCE-CHANGED only when it moves, and returns it as baseRevision. Limits: the nine version 1 Door routes keep the full revision and byte-identical output (the version 1 records operation leaves authoredRevision out), and MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and ia scope are unchanged; admission's findings and the database's seat and root decisions still read every placement, so a runtime-band record that an authored loaded record names can still move a body's unknowns, and one that changes which authored records are admitted (one repeating an authored requirement id refuses both) leaves a capture untrusted, no-capture, until the next ia capture; and `ia validate` and `ia-distribution validate` now write .ia/work/evidence/<authoredRevision>.ia at runtime placement, which only a reader opened with evidence lists and no shipped reader opens that way, so for every shipped reader only the locations override places a source there.

changes.title: `ia preview` and `ia author` admit checks structurally, as `ia validate` does
changes.summary: @inventarch/cli: `ia preview` and `ia author` open their editor snapshot with structural check admission (plan amendment C21), as `ia validate` and `ia-distribution validate` open their session. A `@check` whose check.runs or check.implementation names one evaluator that is not built in is admitted there: an existing one is an owned record the edit forms can name, where the strict snapshot answered IA-CLI-EDIT-MISSING, and a new one previews clean and is written, where the strict snapshot counted IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN against the candidate and `ia author` refused it with IA-CLI-EDIT-UNCLEAN. A check naming no evaluator still counts against the candidate as IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN. Neither command lists or reads runtime evidence: the snapshot holds no record at runtime placement, and the base revision a preview prints is the evidence-free one every strict reader reports, while an evidence file for that authored revision exists. @inventarch/db: the ./editor subpath adds EditorOptions, which extends InputOptions with checks ('strict', the default, or 'structural', the values and default of OpenOptions.checks). EditorDatabase(root, options) and EditorSnapshot(input, changes, options) accept it, and a structural editor database's snapshot, its preview drafts, its candidates and every update or refresh admit structurally. A caller that passes no checks option keeps strict admission, as every other editor caller does. Limits: every other reader of the admitted graph stays strict, as the structural check admission note lists. Once `ia author` writes such a check, every strict reader counts it as an IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN error: ia host and ia project refuse the workspace (IA-CLI-CONFLICT, exit 3), ia capture still writes its snapshot with the finding recorded and exits 1, and ia validate's summary names the check.

changes.title: `ia validate` binds every `@check` and records the bound ones that passed or failed as runtime `@observation` evidence
changes.summary: Plan amendments C14, C15, C22 and C23. @inventarch/db adds bindChecks(records, report, catalog), checkVerdicts(verdicts, runner, scope, excluded?), WHOLE_WORKSPACE_SCOPE ('*'), the CheckBinding, CheckBindingStatus, CheckCatalog and CheckOutcome types, EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY ('.ia/work/evidence'), EVIDENCE_FILE, CHECK_EVIDENCE_WORD, evidenceText, readEvidence, writeEvidence (with an optional pruneBefore) with the EvidenceObservation and EvidenceWrite types, InputOptions.evidence, InputSnapshot.evidence (candidates listed by path, size and modification time) and the EvidenceCandidate type. COMP-CHECK's pass for a check only structural admission admits counts as not-evaluated. A built-in evaluator is always bound, with the aggregate of the admission verdicts its text check.scope selects: every one for the documented whole-workspace token *, otherwise exactly the verdicts whose scope equals it; fail dominates, then not-evaluated, then pass, and an empty selection (a prose or unknown scope, or an evaluator that reported nothing) is not-evaluated, never a pass. Any other evaluator binds against the evaluators section of the catalog the workspace's host joined, through the same trust and joined catalog as execution bindings: unavailable without a catalog, when the catalog does not list it, lists it unavailable or is not valid, revoked (an error) when it revokes it or failed verification, and bound but never invoked, so not-evaluated, when it supports it, since no host implementation runs an evaluator in this release. A payload without a catalog, such as 2.0.0's, leaves every catalog check unavailable, never revoked. @inventarch/distribution adds WorkspaceSession.checks(trust) with the ValidationChecks type, SessionOptions with checks, WorkspaceSession.openedAt, WorkspaceAdmission.authoredRevision and recordValidation(session, checks), the one writer of evidence; WorkspaceSession.validation(), bindings() and checks() still read only, and a session never reads evidence, so what a validation admits, binds, counts and exits with is the authored view alone and its revision is the one every other reader reports, as in 2.0.0. Behavior change: ia validate and ia-distribution validate, until now read-only, write .ia/work/evidence/<authored revision>.ia whenever a bound check passed or failed: one `@observation` per such check, named <check name>-<12 hex authored revision>, verdict success or refusal, at runtime placement band 0, staged and renamed into place, the same bytes on a second validate at one authored revision, and the files of other authored revisions pruned best effort (a file the process may not remove, or one modified after the run read its inputs, is kept, and pruning never refuses); a not-evaluated check records nothing, a workspace without the `@observation` word records nothing, and a validation whose admission is refused records and prunes nothing; since a failing built-in verdict always refuses admission, ia validate never writes a refusal observation in this release. Evidence never moves the authored revision, the position packet, the host projection or what any other reader admits: only a reader opened with evidence reads the current authored revision's file, and only when its admission is not refused and the writer, binding that reader's own checks again and taking the times from the file itself, reproduces it byte for byte (so a forged verdict, reason, record or time, an observation for a check not evaluated, a relationship or any other byte is not evidence) and adding it changes nothing the authored records admit; db exports reproducesEvidence for that test. The writer keeps an observation's first times only from such a file; a time not in the writer's exact stamp, with observed and captured apart, or more than five minutes ahead of the reading clock is not evidence; any other time is carried as written, not verified. A current file found unchanged is touched, so a validation of another revision that began earlier never prunes it. Where this revision's evidence must be written and cannot be (a read-only checkout) both validations now refuse, before anything is pruned, ia validate with IA-DIST-EVIDENCE-UNWRITABLE at exit 3, and a link, junction or file at .ia/work or .ia/work/evidence refuses as IA-DB-PATH-UNSAFE; nothing is ever read through one, and with nothing to record neither validation refuses for it; a CI job that validated a read-only tree with passing checks under 2.0.0 must make .ia/work writable. ia validate's human report adds a Checks section (the catalog source when a check needs one, one entry per check with its evaluator, binding, outcome and reason, and what was recorded) and summary lines for revoked and not-evaluated checks, and closes with a not-evaluated note when a check was not evaluated; --json adds checks and evidence, and ia-distribution validate adds both to its result; a revoked check exits 1. --json adds authoredRevision beside revision. ia doctor, ia capture --preview and refused effects never create or prune evidence. Limits: no evaluator runs, the host registers no evaluator codec, and only built-in evaluators produce evidence.

changes.title: A `@check` can claim paths with `check.covers`; `check.scope` stays text and claims none
changes.summary: Plan amendments C17 and C22. compliance-system's `@check` schema gains an optional check.covers, a list of text path selections, and documents check.scope, still required text, as what the check selects (the whole-workspace token *, a scope its evaluator reports, or prose). @inventarch/graph adds check.covers to CLAIM_FIELDS, so the claimant index, claimants(graph, path), db resolveSeat's claimants, db inertDeclarations, ia position's location seats and every other reader of claimants name a check whose covers selects a path, with field check.covers; a check's check.scope is still never a claim, even text that reads as a path, and claiming a path changes nothing about which verdicts ia validate binds the check to. A workspace that states no check.covers sees no change apart from its revision, which moves with the new schema bytes. The public vocabulary (docs/reference/language/vocabulary.json and .md, the CLI and door catalogues), the generated authoring reference for `@check` (shipped in @inventarch/authoring-system) and the authoring resource manifest are regenerated, and @inventarch/compliance-system ships the new schema, and the bundled inventarch/language base and the embedded host payload are rebuilt from the new schema, which moves the host payload pin. The coordinated native transition selects 2.1.0 for all twelve native archives, including inventarch/language, compliance-system and authoring-system. The native release ledger and gate preserve published id@version bytes and require content-driven version selection against the immutable published baseline; this release does not replace the published 1.2.0 bytes. Native versions remain independent from the npm cohort. Admission follows the schema bytes a workspace has installed, not the CLI reading it: a workspace still on the 2.0.0 base (inventarch/language 1.2.0 with the old bytes) cannot state check.covers, under any CLI, until its base moves, and a reader older than this release admits the field where the workspace's base declares it but does not treat it as a claim.

changes.title: `ia author` applies previewed permitted record edits with digest checks
changes.summary: @inventarch/cli adds `ia author` (catalog row: mode author, move Synthesis) for permitted record words. It accepts the corresponding preview arguments and --digest <sha256>, the target file digest printed by the preview. It compiles the candidate again against one editor snapshot, applies the author-mode mandate profile, and writes only when the digest still identifies the current file and the candidate is clean. Existing files use an opened-handle recheck and guarded temporary-file replacement; new files use create-only publication. The edit preserves surrounding records, line endings, a byte-order mark and existing permission bits. One attribution comment records the acting participant, a governing mandate granting Synthesis and the authored revision; a later author replaces that comment rather than stacking it. Attribution and --actor are local declarations, not authentication. The final integrated source-protection boundary refuses author mutations of workspace, agent, mandate, system, schema, agent-profile and hook records for every actor, including an ungoverned actor. This covers creation, field edits and relationship edits, so `ia author system` does not write a starter system and changing actors does not bypass this administrative-word boundary. Existing profile, ownership and binding-mandate refusals keep precedence. Previews remain read-only; direct owner source edits followed by validation remain the administrative path. The separate administrative-authoring note describes this breaking boundary and doctor warnings. Every successful author command names a profile-judged next command. Refusals retain preview's diagnostics, plus missing or malformed --digest (IA-CLI-USAGE, exit 2), changed input (IA-CLI-EDIT-STALE, exit 1), an unclean candidate (IA-CLI-EDIT-UNCLEAN, exit 1), and distribution or volume failures (exit 3). A refusal writes nothing. One record, row or field is written per invocation, and `ia author` does not execute operations. Mandates and these CLI refusals are cooperative restrictions, not filesystem isolation: a direct file edit remains possible, and a source-protection declaration alone does not prove that a host enforces it.

changes.title: Consumer commands are judged by the acting participant's `@mandate` profile; `ia position` stays ungated
changes.summary: Breaking: @inventarch/cli now judges `ia read` and `ia next` (move Observation), `ia validate` and `ia preview` (Verification), `ia author` (Synthesis), and `ia capture`, its `ia compile` alias, `ia project` and a workspace `ia host <host> --apply`, which writes the same projection (Execution), by the acting participant's mandate profile (runtime governingMandates, defaultActor and profileRefusal) before they read or write anything; a capture or project plan is judged as the effect it plans, while a host plan, `ia host --remove` (which restores editing) and `ia host claude --user` are not judged. Where 2.0.0 ran these commands unconditionally, five cases now refuse them at exit 1: authored mandates that do not grant the mode's move, or, for preview and author only, exclude the word they write (IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-MOVE, -WORD); several authored participants and no authored `composition.steward`, an installed steward counting as none (IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR); a default actor, such as an authored steward the mandates do not name, that no governing mandate binds (IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR); an admitted governing mandate the runtime cannot read, such as one with a child under `authority.moves`, which admission accepts (IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID, located at the mandate); and, whatever the actor, path or word, any authored `@mandate` that failed admission, a stated `authority.moves []` among them, or a refused `@agent` or `@workspace` an admitted mandate or workspace depends on, which admission now refuses (IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID located at that record, described in the mandate-admission note). `ia preview` and `ia author` also judge the mandates whose authority.covers selects the target file. As in the edit guard, the selection and the path are both keyed with db pathKey before the G06c match, so on win32 and darwin, where pathKey folds case whatever the volume, a covers entry claims the file in any letter case, including a covered directory that does not exist yet and an entry cased differently from the directory on disk, and on a case-sensitive directory there it also claims a sibling spelled in another case; on other platforms case is significant. A workspace `ia init` creates grants all five moves to its one participant, so the mandate-profile layer allows its commands as before; a workspace with no governing mandate adds no restriction at that layer. The integrated administrative-authoring boundary still refuses workspace, agent, mandate, system, schema, agent-profile and hook mutations for every actor, including an ungoverned actor, as described in the administrative-authoring note. `ia position` and every command outside those modes are not gated, so the governance position a refusal names always runs (a refusal at a record admission refused names the admission report, the machine route `ia report`, which no mandate gates, instead; see the mandate-admission note for how its root is spelled); neither are the Door's read, next and position operations (the MCP tools), the install, update and remove projection refresh, `ia-distribution validate`, `ia inspect` and the records route, `ia init`, and `ia host`'s plan, `--remove` and `--user`. Each gated command accepts --actor <agent> (a canonical identity, `@agent <name>` or a bare name), which must be an authored participant of the repository's `@workspace`: an authored `@agent` a mandate scoped to it names, or its `composition.steward` when that is an authored `@agent`; an installed steward is no default actor. Naming an actor is a local declaration, not authentication, accepted whether or not the workspace leaves the choice open: it resolves an open choice, or under a steward acts as another of the workspace's actors, and then that participant's own mandates are judged, which may be looser or stricter than the default actor's; it never lifts a move or excluded word those mandates state. Every refusal names one command that runs for the same actor in the same state: the governance position of the mandate concerned (for a record admission refused, the admission report `ia report`); under an open choice, or for a default actor no governing mandate binds, the same command with --actor naming the first participant whose mandates allow it (for an `ia author` form without a usable --digest, its `ia preview` form, which prints the digest); for an --actor that names no participant, the same command without it where the default actor may run it (for an `ia author` form without a usable --digest, again its `ia preview` form). Once a command's profile allows it, a refusal it raises later is held to the same rule: a next command of a gated mode the profile refuses becomes the governance position, and one it allows carries the named --actor. `ia project --apply` and a workspace `ia host --apply` write the rendering their gated plan session made, planned again against the files: a file changed since the plan still refuses, but a source or mandate change made while the confirmation question waits is not picked up, and `ia doctor` then reports the projection outdated. The machine routes, every `ia scope` form, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and the runtime's own refusals are unchanged. Limits: actor selection is not host authentication; a mandate restricts only the gated CLI commands, not the ungated surfaces above; the next-command rule holds for gated commands only, so an ungated command's refusal may name a gated command that then refuses with its own mandate refusal; the edit guard re-keyed to `@mandate`, which reads the same resolver, is described in its own note (generation-hook-governance).

changes.title: `ia preview` shows what one new record, field or relationship would compile to
changes.summary: @inventarch/cli adds `ia preview` (catalog row: mode validate, move Verification), which writes nothing. `ia preview <word> <name> [<field>=<value>...] [--at <path>]` drafts a new record into --at or <first authored root>/<word>.ia, the first root the repository's `@workspace` declares at authored placement inside .ia/src (`ia preview system <name>` is init's starter system at .ia/src/systems/<name>/system.ia); `ia preview --relate <owned> <spelling> <target>` adds one relationship row and `ia preview --set <owned> <section.key>=<value>` sets one field (`+=` adds one item to a list field) of an owned record: one at authored placement (band 100) in a file under such a root, outside the floor, named by canonical identity or `@word name`. --at must lie under such a root and is judged as the volume spells it: an existing part of the path spelled otherwise (a case variant, an 8.3 short name) is refused, naming the volume's spelling, before the mandate profile or the ownership check reads it. A field is <section>.<key> or a key one schema field alone has; one given twice in either spelling is refused, and a value the shell split is joined again with single spaces. The edit is language's, spliced into the file as it is (other lines keep their bytes and line endings, a byte-order mark stays), and compiled through db's draft overlay against one editor snapshot of the workspace; the output gives the record before and after, the base and candidate revisions, every record of the file with its digest before and after, the file's current sha256 (an absent file reads as empty) and the findings that count against the candidate: the edited or new record's own and any the base does not hold, so an error already in another record or file does not. A record other than the target whose digest would change refuses the preview. `ia preview <word>` prints the word's lowering, schema, default file and consent. Exit 0 for a clean candidate or word guidance, 1 for a candidate with errors. Refusals: a malformed form or an unknown relationship verb is IA-CLI-USAGE at exit 2; IA-CLI-EDIT-INVALID (an unknown word or field, a value of another type or carrying syntax, a field given twice, a duplicate, a nested record, a system already in force), IA-CLI-EDIT-MISSING (no admitted record answers a name), IA-CLI-EDIT-UNOWNED (an installed, adopted or floor record, or a path outside the authored roots), IA-CLI-EDIT-MANDATE (a `@mandate` that binds the acting participant, before or after the edit (its participant is the actor, or it names none and its scope names the workspace or it claims paths), or whose authority the runtime cannot read, naming the governance position) and IA-LANG-EDGE-UNCONSENTED (a row the two-sided consent rule refuses, naming the system whose ledger refuses it) exit 1; IA-DB-PATH-UNSAFE (another spelling of a path, an unsafe path, one holding DEL, a C1 control, a line or paragraph separator or a bidirectional control included, or a link on the way), IA-DB-SOURCE-UNAVAILABLE, IA-DB-SOURCE-CHANGED, IA-DB-DRAFT-INVALID and a workspace that does not open exit 3. A refusal's next command that would repeat a value holding shell syntax ($(...), a backtick, %, a quote, ;) names the word's preview instead; only the invocation's own --root value, as the option before any --, is exempt, and a bare argument opening a comment (#) or a PowerShell splat (@), or holding a comma (a PowerShell array) or a tilde past its start, is repeated double-quoted, while one opening with a tilde, which pwsh expands even double-quoted through an npm-style .ps1 shim, is never repeated. Limits: every printed command repeats the --root value as given, double-quoted only when it holds a space or a quote, so a root path holding a comma or a tilde is printed bare. `ia next` on a workspace that registers `@plan` and authors none names `ia preview plan` where the acting participant's profile allows it, instead of the records to author. The position packet's command catalog gains preview and author rows alongside the integrated command set; the repository's own CLAUDE.md is regenerated from that catalog. A host projection written by 2.0.0 therefore differs from the packet the CLI now renders: after the upgrade `ia doctor` reports it outdated until `ia project <host> --apply`, or `ia host <host> --apply` for a registered host, rewrites it (review C2-N6). Limits: nested records and conditional, structured or internally commented fields are not edited; the --root value is repeated in next commands as every command repeats it; the mandate profile it consults is described in its own note.

changes.title: replace and createFile remove their temporary file when a write fails
changes.summary: @inventarch/distribution's replace and createFile (the publishers `ia author` writes through) now remove their temporary sibling file when opening it succeeds and the permission change, the write or the fsync then fails, as they already did when the rename or link failed; before, such a failure left a `<target>.<uuid>.tmp` file beside the target. The published file, its permission bits and the IA-DIST-LOCAL-MODIFICATION refusal for an entry that appeared are unchanged. Limits: neither publisher locks its target, so a writer that saves the file between a caller's last read and the rename is still replaced; a caller narrows that window by reading the file through an opened handle just before, as ia author does, but cannot close it.

changes.title: `ia validate` reports each `@execution-binding` as bound, unavailable or revoked against the catalog its host joined
changes.summary: @inventarch/workspace-runtime adds the ./bind subpath (and ./internal/bind), exporting executionBindings(reader), executionBindingOf(record, resolve?) and bindExecution(binding, catalog) with the ExecutionBinding, BindingTarget, BindingCatalog, BindingResult and BindingStatus types; a present BindingCatalog's operation rows are @inventarch/db/distribution's InstalledOperation, the catalog's one shape. executionBindings reads every admitted `@execution-binding` in the root view, sorted by identity, with its unconditional binding.kind, binding.implementation and binding.target, a stated target kept as the reference written and the identity of the admitted record it resolves to (null when none answers it, and without a resolver), so a stated target is never read as no target. bindExecution returns bound only when the catalog is present, lists the implementation as available, the binding is of kind operation and its target, when it states one, resolves to the operation the implementation serves; unavailable when the binding names no implementation, its kind has no catalog section (only operation implementations are listed), the catalog is unavailable, does not list the implementation or lists it unavailable, the stated target resolves to no admitted record, or the implementation serves another operation; the canonical read-captured-source-binding therefore reports unavailable in an ia init consumer, which admits no `@operation` read-captured-source; and revoked, an error, when the catalog revokes the implementation or failed verification. @inventarch/distribution adds joinedCatalog(root, trust) with the JoinedCatalog type (a damaged one names the payload directory, whose deletion and a host re-apply are the repair) and the HostTrust type ({home, release}: the validating installation's IA home and the payload release it pins) and installationTrust(), the trust of the distribution module's own installation (the host payload it runs from, or null outside one). joinedCatalog opens only <home>/hosts/<release>: a join counts only when it and its host's registration name the pinned release and the registration names that payload directory, so a registration of another release or of a payload anywhere else (another IA home, inside the workspace, a network path) is unavailable with the repair ia host <host> --apply, and nothing it names is opened. It reads that payload once, reports it damaged when it fails verification with changed or unlisted files, a link, exceeded limits or a release.json that does not hash to the pin, parseable or not, whichever trusted join names it, takes the first trusted join in consumer order that carries its catalog digest, and is unavailable with the reasons when there is no receipt, no trust or no trusted join that holds (an ia project-only workspace, a host registered by another release, a drifted join, a payload without a catalog or not materialized); WorkspaceSession gains bindings(trust), with the ValidationBindings type, which returns that catalog source (null when the workspace has no binding, and then nothing beyond the records is read) and one result per binding, and ia-distribution validate, passing installationTrust(), adds it to its result as bindings and exits 1 when a binding is revoked. @inventarch/cli's ia validate reports the same bindings, trusting the payload its bundled host pin names in the IA home IA_HOME or IA_HOST_HOME resolves (or, run from inside a payload, that payload): --json adds bindings, and the human report adds a Bindings section with the catalog source and one row per binding, a summary line counting unbound bindings as not a pass, and revoked bindings as errors that fail the run and the closing line; a workspace with no binding keeps its human report unchanged. ia doctor's implementations row names a revoked operation and warns. Computing and reporting bindings writes nothing, in the workspace or the IA home. Limits: binding inspection and reporting do not load, import, serve or execute implementations. The separate local runner host binds and executes its fixed installed captured-read operation under the selected mandate and bounded runtime; only the catalog may revoke, since the `@execution-binding` schema has no revocation field; entry, hook and other non-operation bindings are always unavailable because the catalog lists no implementations of those kinds; a damaged joined payload revokes every operation binding, whatever implementation it names, while a missing payload file makes them unavailable; and ia validate's findings, counts, admission status and report outcome are unchanged, so a revoked binding fails the run without appearing among the findings.

changes.title: workspace-runtime generates a claude agent file for each authored `@agent-profile`, or reports why it does not
changes.summary: @inventarch/workspace-runtime adds the ./internal/generate subpath, which exports generateAgentProfiles(reader, within, host) with the GeneratedFile, GeneratedSet, GeneratedWord and UnsupportedRecord types. It returns a frozen {files, unsupported}. Only `@agent-profile` records at band 100 (authored by the workspace) that the scope token admits are read, by identity; one below band 100, where an installed or adopted base places the public vocabulary, renders nothing and is not reported, and a workspace that authors public systems renders their profiles. For codex every authored profile is an unsupported row {identity, word: 'agent-profile', reason}, because a codex agent needs an entry in .codex/config.toml, which holds the owned MCP block. For claude each profile renders {path, text, identity, word: 'agent-profile'} at .claude/agents/<profile name>.md, except that a profile is an unsupported row naming the reason, and the others still render, when its name is not a portable host name (lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens, a letter first and no hyphen last, at most 64 characters, no Windows device name including com0 and lpt0), when its capabilities allow no host tool (claude gives an agent with no tool list every tool, so no file is written), when the composition compiler would refuse its capability closure (its capabilities include one another in a cycle, or an included capability has an effect its includer does not declare), or when its text is not inert prose (no executable dynamic context such as !`cmd`, no active HTML, no unbalanced code span or fence), which is judged on each authored value before it is rendered, so the reason names what the record itself holds, and again on the rendered file. A profile's capability closure is its composition.capabilities and every capability they include through composition.includes, each once. The text is YAML frontmatter (the JSON-quoted name; a description taken from the meaning.says of its composition.agent when the workspace authors that agent, otherwise the profile's own; and tools, the claude names of the host tools the effects of the profile's own composition.capabilities cover through the prose profiles' effect table, where read covers Read, Glob and Grep and no other effect maps a tool, as one comma-separated string; the compiler holds each capability's own effects as the ceiling of what it includes, so the included capabilities add no tool), then the marker `<!-- Generated by ia project; edit the cited native records. -->` on its own line, then a body naming the profile and its agent, with a Mandate section, a Voice section when composition.voice is set, a Tools section with one line per capability of the closure naming its operations, effects and host tools, and a Delegates section with one line per composition.delegates reference. The Mandate section holds the profile's own composition.mandate as one list item with its authority fields (participant, moves, scope, excluded words, covers) and execution.limit-* fields nested beneath it, as authored; when that mandate names a participant other than the profile's agent, a nested line says so, and that the edit guard and the CLI's mandate profile judge the agent by the mandates that bind it. A profile that names no mandate falls back to the authored mandates @inventarch/runtime's governingMandates says bind its composition.agent (those that name it, and those that name no participant and state a scope or covers; one that states neither governs no path and is left out), each as such a group under a line labelling them as the fallback and saying the guard refuses the agent where a mandate that binds another participant governs and none of these grants the move; the line says when none binds, and says the fallback is unavailable, with the reason, when a mandate's authority cannot be read or the agent is not admitted, without failing the render; the fallback is resolved only for a rendered profile that needs it. Free text is written as the position packet writes it: on one line, each bare IA word a code span in the body, C0 and C1 controls, Unicode line separators and bidirectional controls as spaces, `<!--` written `<!--`, a `!` that a rendered code span would follow written `!`, and a leading `<` written `<`, so no value opens a comment, reads as dynamic context or opens an HTML block. A reference no admitted record in the scope answers is printed as authored, and the agent, mandate, voice and capability lines, whose records' fields would be read, say it is not admitted in this scope (a delegate, an operation and a participant are printed as authored only). The bytes depend only on the records: no absolute path, time, scope token or revision. An unknown host is refused with IA-PROJECTION-INPUT-INVALID, and for either host an unknown or stale scope token keeps its database code. Limits: the frontmatter names no model; conditional field values are not rendered.

changes.title: The edit guard returns, re-keyed to the `@mandate` that governs the edited path, with one owned hook group per authored `@hook`
changes.summary: This reverses milestone 5's B11 retirement of the guard at the mechanism level. @inventarch/steward-hook: the guard entry (runHook, and the host launcher's guard mode, which passes its arguments through) also accepts `--root <absolute root> --hook <identity>`, and evaluateMandateHook(root, hook, event) and printable(text) are exported. In that mode, for every edit tool whatever the hook names, the input checks, path safety and managed-state protection of the existing guard run first: installation state, owned projection files and, while a hook or guard registration is owned, the two Claude settings files and the cache launcher are refused with IA-HOOK-PROJECTION-MANAGED; the retired steward rule for .ia/src/systems/<name>/ is not applied and is not a fallback. In both guard modes a win32 path naming an alternate data stream (a : after the drive) is refused with IA-HOOK-PATH-UNSAFE, and in `--hook` mode so is a file with more than one hard link wherever it is under the root, selected or not (a pnpm store link included), since another of its names may be selected. The named hook must be one admitted authored (band 100) `@hook` that hook generation declares (PreToolUse; Write, Edit or MultiEdit; one or more workspace-relative path selections written with /; a non-blank message). Otherwise the registration refuses, with IA-HOOK-DECLARATION-UNAVAILABLE, the edits under the selection last registered for it (which the hook ownership state records), or every edit under the root when none is recorded; it does the same, with IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE, when the workspace's records cannot be read at all (a descriptor the db cannot read, a lock rewritten with CRLF line ends). Each such refusal names only commands that work from a shell in that state: `ia host claude --root <root> --remove --apply --yes`, which removes the registration and restores editing and needs neither an admitting workspace nor readable records; where the workspace admits, `ia host claude --root <root> --apply --yes`, which registers its current hooks; and where it does not, `ia validate --root <root>`, which shows why, or, where the records were read and an authored `@mandate`, or a record an admitted mandate or workspace depends on, is among what admission refused, the admission report (`ia report --root <root>`, the root printed only when every character of it is inert unquoted, else `ia report` from the workspace root), since `ia validate` then refuses. When the database cannot open at all, that last command is `ia validate --root <root>`; when it opens but its records then cannot be read, the admission read first decides between the two. When the hook ownership state itself cannot be read, which the removal refuses too, the refusal names that state's repair instead: delete the state file and every IA hook group in .claude/settings.local.json from a shell, then run the removal. A hook decides an edit only when its hook.tools name the event's tool and its hook.paths select the file; any other edit is allowed. Nothing is decided because it lies under .ia/src: a workspace protects its governing records by selecting them in a hook, such as `paths [".ia/src/**"]`. The actor is established first. An event carrying agent_id is a subagent acting as the composition.agent of the one authored `@agent-profile` named exactly its agent_type; an unknown subagent, a malformed agent_id or a subagent without agent_type is refused with IA-HOOK-IDENTITY-UNAVAILABLE at every path the hook selects, governed or not. Any other event, including a main session launched with --agent (agent_type without agent_id), acts as the default actor (composition.steward, else its single participant) of the `@workspace` ia position seats the path in. A selected edit is governed by the mandates @inventarch/runtime's governingMandates returns for the path and that workspace: those whose authority.covers claims the path, and those scoped to the workspace. With none it is allowed. Otherwise it is allowed when profileRefusal allows the author mode (Synthesis) for the actor, a mandate that names no participant binding every established actor, and refused with IA-HOOK-NOT-MANDATED, the hook's message and the next command ia position --seat <mandate> --shape governance. A main session whose default actor is ambiguous, or that has none while a governing mandate names a participant, is IA-HOOK-IDENTITY-UNAVAILABLE. A refusal of the main session also names `ia host claude --root <root> --remove --apply --yes`, which removes every hook group and needs neither an admitting workspace nor readable records. An admitted governing mandate whose authority cannot be read is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE naming its governance position, unreadable records are IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE naming the commands above, a failure while the edit is decided is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE naming the admission report, and while any authored `@mandate`, or a record an admitted mandate or workspace depends on, fails admission every selected edit, and every edit of a registration whose hook is not admitted (the hook may share the refused mandate's file), is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE naming the refused record's path:line and the admission report (described in the mandate-admission note; `ia validate`, mandate-gated, would refuse there), and a selected path reached through a link, a junction or a short name is IA-HOOK-PATH-UNSAFE. hook.paths and authority.covers are matched in the G06c dialect (only *, ? and / are special) with db pathKey applied to both sides, so on win32 and darwin, where pathKey folds case whatever the volume, DOCS/x.md is under docs/** and Docs/** (on a case-sensitive directory there, a sibling spelled in another case is selected or claimed too), and on other platforms case is significant. Refusal reasons are printed without terminal escape sequences, C0 or C1 controls, line separators or bidirectional controls, and bounded. @inventarch/runtime: HOOK_CODES gains IA-HOOK-DECLARATION-UNAVAILABLE, IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE and IA-HOOK-NOT-MANDATED; the package root exports evaluateMandateGuard(handle, within, request), mandateGuardSelects(request) and seatedWorkspace(handle, within, path) with the MandateGuardRequest and MandateGuardDecision types, and the ./internal/mandate-guard subpath serves the guard module; the ./internal/packet subpath also exports fieldsAt, valuesAt, textsAt and stated, the field readers the packet and the host generators share; GoverningOptions gains an optional fold key, and without it governingMandates is unchanged. @inventarch/distribution: the ./guard-registration subpath exports HOOK_TOOLS, hookStatePath, hookGroup, savedHooks, planHookRegistration(root, {cache, hooks} | {remove}), planHooksFor(root, expected, hooks), applyHookRegistration(plan, checkpoint?), readHookRegistration(root, id?), observeHookRegistration(root, id?), hookGroupDigest(group) and hooksDisabledBy(root) with the HookRow, HookTool, HookRequest, HookAction, HookPlan, HookState, OwnedHook, HookDrift and Group types. They keep one PreToolUse group per hook row {identity, tools, paths} in .claude/settings.local.json, whose matcher is always Write|Edit|MultiEdit (the row's tools are validated, and the guard applies them to the hook's paths from the record) and whose handler runs `guard --root <root> --hook <identity>` in the retired guard's fixed derivation. The groups are owned by exact match against .ia/distributions/hosts/claude-hooks-<id>.json (ia.hook-registration-state.v1), which also records each hook's registered paths; they are published under the host lock through guard-pending.json (format ia.hook-registration-pending.v1) and recovered by recoverGuardRegistration (recover-guard), which reads either journal format. With disableAllHooks on, a plan that would create or update a group refuses, and one that only keeps or removes owned groups proceeds. Unrelated groups, keys and bytes are kept; a re-plan of the same rows writes nothing; a changed cache replaces the owned group in place, a changed selection updates only the ownership state, and a changed tool list neither (the guard reads the tools from the record); and removing the last hook removes only its groups, the containers the first registration created and a file it created, so the settings return to their original bytes only when nothing else in them changed meanwhile, and a container the groups emptied that existed before is written as [] or {} whatever whitespace it held. An owned group deleted, changed or duplicated by hand is refused with IA-DIST-LOCAL-MODIFICATION, naming the way back: for a changed or duplicated group, delete only that group, then remove the registration (`ia host claude --remove --apply`) and register it again. guardNode takes an optional hook identity; assertRetirableGuard and the retired guard's removal ignore groups that name --hook, so a 1.x steward-guard registration is still only ever removed; and the launcher's guard mode description names --hook. Limits: how ia host, ia project and ia init register the groups is described with the projection writer's change; Codex hooks remain unsupported; excluded words are not enforced by the guard (record authoring enforces them); the guard reads records, not file bytes, and a mandate grants no host permission; Claude Code on win32 runs the direct form, which still fails open when its Node cannot start; the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and every ia scope form are unchanged.

changes.title: `ia host` applies the generated agents, skills and `@hook` groups through the one projection writer, and its receipt lists them
changes.summary: @inventarch/cli: `ia host <claude|codex>` and `ia init --host` render the position packet together with the files and hooks generated from the workspace's authored records, computed once, and apply exactly that set through the one projection writer: for claude one .claude/agents/<name>.md per authored `@agent-profile` and one .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md per authored `@playbook`, each with the packet marker, and one hook group per authored `@hook` in .claude/settings.local.json; for codex one .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md per playbook, every profile and hook reported as not taken. One apply retires a 1.x steward guard, then registers or removes the hook groups against the payload `ia host` materializes and verifies, then writes the files, then the receipt. `ia host <host> --remove --apply` no longer requires an admitting workspace or records that open: it renders nothing and removes the registration, its hook groups and its files whatever the records say. A record renamed or deleted takes its obsolete agent file, skill or group away on the next apply; unrelated settings keys and groups and unmarked files are kept; a second apply changes no file, setting or state and writes the same receipt rows. `ia project`, the install, update and remove refresh and a migration keep the groups an earlier `ia host` registration owns in step with the records, against the payload that registration recorded, writing nothing and not reading that payload while the owned hooks and selections are the declared ones, and refusing at that payload, naming `ia host claude --apply`, when a change needs it and it is gone or changed; with no registration they register none and list each declared hook as not taken. The receipt gains generated (record identity, word, path and SHA-256 of each generated file), definitions (each authored `@operation` with its handler and validator ids copied as authored and never resolved or run, and each `@harness` with the agents, skills and hooks it registers, as that apply wrote and registered them: a hook it did not register, for want of a payload, is not listed), hooks (each owned group by `@hook` identity, the tools the hook declares and the group's SHA-256) and unsupported (each authored record the host does not take, with the reason); removedHooks lists each hook group an apply removed, by `@hook` identity and the SHA-256 it was last registered with, an interrupted earlier apply's included; removed also lists the generated files an apply deleted; a receipt without these sections still reads. An install, update or remove plans the refresh's files and hook step before its first install write, and `ia init --migrate` checks the hook step before it plans: an owned hook group deleted, changed or duplicated by hand, a recorded payload a change of hooks would need, or a generated skill refused at a populated folder of the user's refuses there, never after the install commits (any other file refusal stays the refresh's, as before), and the install preview lists a generated agent as the refresh writes it, never as a 1.x file to remove. Where disableAllHooks turns hooks off, no group is written: a group already owned for a hook still declared stays registered; an obsolete owned group is removed (an `ia host` apply that materializes the payload the kept groups were registered against plans the removal against it, in its preview too), or, when that payload is gone and not materialized, kept and reported as kept (never as registered, and as one row with generation's reason for an unsupported authored hook) until hooks are back on or that payload is materialized again; a group changed or duplicated by hand refuses as it does with hooks on, and so does one deleted by hand whose hook is still declared, while a deleted group of a hook no longer declared loses its ownership in the next plan that runs (with the payload gone and not materialized it waits as the kept groups do, and doctor reports the group missing); and each authored hook with no group is reported as not taken, naming the settings file, while the MCP entry, the packet, the agents and the skills apply as before (a 2.0.0 apply did not refuse there either). The plans of `ia host` and `ia project` list each hook group's action (create, update, unchanged or remove) and each record not taken. A generation refusal keeps its own code and names ia validate. `ia doctor` adds a row for each owned hook group that is missing (deleted by hand) or modified (changed or duplicated): a fail whose remedy is `ia host claude --remove --apply`, after which `ia host claude --apply` registers the workspace's hooks again, since apply never puts back a group the user took away; a guard group naming --hook that no registration owns is a warning, left in place; an authored `@hook` the last apply could not register is a warning saying it guards nothing, naming `ia host claude --apply` (none when disableAllHooks turned hooks off); a kept obsolete group is a warning saying the next `ia host claude --apply` removes it once hooks are back on, or while they are off once it materializes the payload the group was registered against; and an outdated row when the generated rows differ from the receipt's, a receipt written before generation included. @inventarch/distribution: the ./projection subpath exports GENERATED_PATHS and projectionOwnable(host, path). The planner owns generated files at .claude/agents/<name>.md, .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md through the same ia.host-projection-state.v1 state: an owned one no render writes any more is removed when it still carries an owned marker (a listed skill without one is kept as foreign), along with the skill folder that removal empties (never recursively), a generated skill is refused where its folder already holds files the state does not own, an unmarked or hand-edited file at a generated path is refused and never overwritten or removed, a generated agent is refused (IA-DIST-PATH-UNSAFE) where .claude/agents is a link, and a generated agent at the path of an owned 1.x steward file replaces it as one update, never an update and a remove of the same path. @inventarch/steward-hook: projection protection reads a state that lists generated skills and protects them, as it protects generated agents. Limits: ownership stays in the projection and hook ownership states, never the receipt; Codex agents and hooks remain unsupported; a 2.0.0 CLI cannot plan a workspace this release applied a generated set to until the registration is removed (see the state-evolution note).

changes.title: The packet receipt types gain optional authored-generation sections, and the packet line helpers are shared
changes.summary: @inventarch/runtime exports from the package root the HostHookDeclaration, PacketDefinition, OperationDefinition, HarnessDefinition and RegistrationRow types. PacketReceipt gains five optional sections: generated (GeneratedRow: record identity, word agent-profile or playbook, path and SHA-256 of each generated file), definitions (PacketDefinition rows, a union of {word: 'operation', definition: OperationDefinition} and {word: 'harness', definition: HarnessDefinition}), hooks (HookGroupRow: each registered group's `@hook` identity, the tools that hook declares and the SHA-256 of the group as written), removedHooks (RemovedHookRow: each group an apply removed, by `@hook` identity and the SHA-256 of the group as last registered) and unsupported (UnsupportedRow: identity, word agent-profile, playbook or hook, and reason); HostOutput gains an optional hooks (HostHookDeclaration: identity, event PreToolUse, the edit tools, the path selections and the message). The package root also exports GeneratedRow, HookGroupRow, RemovedHookRow, UnsupportedRow and the word unions GeneratedFileWord, GeneratedRecordWord, DefinitionWord and HookToolName, each stated once. The ./internal/packet-host subpath also exports inline, code and prose, the line folding, code span and IA-word code span helpers the entry file is written with. changes.title: workspace-runtime renders authored playbook skills, hook declarations and operation and harness definitions

changes.title: A 2.0.0 CLI refuses a workspace this release applied a generated set to, until `ia host claude --remove --apply` is run with this release
changes.summary: The projection ownership state keeps its format name, ia.host-projection-state.v1, and now lists the generated agent and skill files beside the packet's, and .claude/settings.local.json holds one IA hook group per authored `@hook`, owned through .ia/distributions/hosts/claude-hooks-<id>.json. A published 2.0.0 @inventarch/cli or @inventarch/distribution on such a workspace: every `ia host claude` plan, apply or removal, `ia project claude` and the install refresh first look for IA guard groups, recognize each hook group by its launcher's guard arguments, find no 2.0.0 guard ownership state for it, and refuse with IA-DIST-LOCAL-MODIFICATION ("An IA guard group has no matching ownership state; remove only that guard group before retiring steward files"), which asks the user to delete IA's own group by hand; a state that lists a generated skill (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md or .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md) is refused as an invalid projection ownership state (IA-DIST-INPUT-INVALID), for codex too; a claude state that lists generated agents and no skill reads each agent as a 1.x steward file and deletes it as legacy. Interrupted applies are refused too: while a hook registration is interrupted, guard-pending.json holds format ia.hook-registration-pending.v1, so 2.0.0 refuses host writes with IA-DIST-RECOVERY-REQUIRED and its `ia recover guard` refuses the journal as an unknown guard recovery format; and an interrupted projection apply leaves pending receipt evidence (<host>-receipt-pending.json) that may list a generated skill's removal or carry removedHooks, which 2.0.0 refuses as invalid evidence (a generated agent's removal passes its check, which admits agent paths), even for its own `--remove`. This release finishes both: `ia recover guard` for the journal, and its next `ia host <host> --apply` for the evidence. Trade-off (review finding H-N9): the state format name is kept rather than bumped. A new name only when generated paths are listed would turn 2.0.0's silent deletion of generated agents into a refusal, but it would also make 2.0.0 refuse every workspace this release applied a generated set to, and the hook groups, which that state does not hold, refuse in 2.0.0 either way. The deletion is accepted because a generated agent is regenerated from its record by this release's next apply. To hand a workspace back to a 2.0.0 CLI: if .ia/distributions/hosts/guard-pending.json exists, first run this release's `ia recover guard`, and if a <host>-receipt-pending.json exists, this release's `ia host <host> --apply`; then run `ia host claude --remove --apply` with this release (and `ia host codex --remove --apply` where codex is registered), which removes the hook groups, their ownership state, the generated files and the receipt, needing neither an admitting workspace nor readable records; then run 2.0.0's `ia host <claude|codex> --apply`. A workspace that authors no `@agent-profile`, `@playbook` or `@hook` gets no generated file or hook group written, so its projection and hook state stay as 2.0.0 reads them; its receipt only gains optional sections, which 2.0.0's reader ignores.

receipts that cannot be read refuse rather than being replaced. ia host claude|codex --apply, and so ia init --host, reads the receipts before writing anything, refusing ones it cannot read with the repair of deleting them, and records the host's join after every element is applied, with the workspace's authored revision as the consumer revision; a removal drops it, and a failure there names the rerun that finishes the set, so an interrupted apply leaves no join or the previous one. ia doctor adds an implementations row for the catalog of the payload this installation pins in the IA home (ok when present, warn when it lists an unavailable or revoked operation, info when the payload carries none or is not materialized, fail when the payload fails verification) and one join-<host> row per recorded join, compared through the trust ia validate binds with (ok when it names the catalog of the payload this installation pins in the IA home and the host's registration names exactly that payload, warn when it is drifted, when the registration names another release or another directory or spelling, which is never opened, or when the host is not registered, unknown when that payload cannot be read or verified or the installation pins none), an info row for a registered host with no join and a fail row for receipts that cannot be read; one verification of each payload serves its host, catalog and join rows, and doctor still writes nothing. Limits: catalog inspection and CLI/distribution projection do not execute installed evaluators or operation handlers. The separate local runner host executes its fixed installed captured-read operation under the selected mandate and bounded runtime; `@check` binding against the evaluators section is described in the check-binding-evidence note; the catalog lists no installed evaluator; a join records which catalog a host registration joined, not that any handler ran; the ia host --json envelope and its human output are unchanged.

changes.title: Language's editor edits one record of a source file in place, and `draftSource` refuses values that would add structure
changes.summary: @inventarch/language/editor exports appendRecord(text, draft), addRelationship(text, identity, spelling, target), setField(text, identity, path, value, schema, append?), annotateRecord(text, identity, comment), encodeValue(field, text, item?), draftValue(field, text), relationshipConsent(registry, word, spelling, target, fragment?) and SourceEditError, with the DraftSchema, DraftField, SourceEditReason and RelationshipConsent types; @inventarch/runtime/editor re-exports those functions, SourceEditError and the four types, with draftSource and VERB_PHRASES, for hosts that may not import the language package. The language root also exports isNumberText, isQualifiedName and isIsoDate, the number, qname and iso-date rules compliance applies, and @inventarch/compliance's value checks now use them (its verdicts are unchanged). Each edit takes one whole .ia file that parses and returns it again with exactly one top-level record, named `@word name`, changed: a draftSource draft appended after one blank line (an empty file gets the draft's pragma, and a last line with no line ending gains one), one row added to the record's relationships section (or a new section at the record's end), one schema field set as <section>.<key> (append adds one item to a list field, creating it when absent), or one comment line put above the record, replacing one there with the same first word. The edit is spliced into the file as it is: every other line keeps its bytes and line ending, a byte-order mark stays, and only the edited record is formatted, in the file's line ending, so only its digest can move; a trailing comment on a one-line field being replaced is kept. encodeValue is the strict, opt-in spelling setField uses: text is always quoted, and every other type must parse as exactly one value of it by the predicates compliance applies (an id and its `in` set, a reference and its `to` word, a qname, a number, a flag, a list of one, the iso-date form), an id, qname or number written quoted being spelled bare, with nothing after it; line breaks, C0 and C1 controls but the tab, DEL, the Unicode line and paragraph separators and the bidirectional embedding, override and isolate controls are refused. A refused edit throws SourceEditError with a closed reason (parse, identity, nested, field, value, repeated, duplicate, spelling, target, structure) and returns no text: an undeclared field, a value of another type, a field, section or record the file states twice, a relationship row the section already holds word for word, a duplicate list item or record, a conditional or structured field, a comment inside a multi-line value being replaced, a nested record, an unknown verb, and a target that is neither a canonical identity nor `@word name` (either with an optional fragment). relationshipConsent judges one row by the two-sided consent rule admission applies and names the refusing side and the system that registers its word. Bug fix: draftSource (and so @inventarch/runtime/editor's EditorWorkspace.draft) spells each value through draftValue, which writes it as 2.0.0 did (text quoted, every other type as given) but refuses a value that would add structure: a line break still throws a plain Error, as in 2.0.0, and a `when` condition, a comment, or a string, prose or list the value opens and does not close (which would join the rows after it into this one), all of which 2.0.0 wrote into the draft, throws SourceEditError; draftValue called alone refuses a line break with SourceEditError too, and EditorWorkspace.draft reports a SourceEditError as EditorError 'invalid'. appendRecord leaves the file's existing bytes as they are, the last line's own ending included in a file of mixed endings; only the lines it adds take the file's ending. Limits: only top-level records are edited; a relationship row that differs from one already there only in spelling (a canonical identity for a reference, a different case) is left to admission; consent and admission are the caller's to compile and report (no IA-LANG diagnostic code is added); the file must parse, and only the edited record is reformatted.

changes.title: Run native profiles with bounded local execution and durable journals
changes.summary: Add @inventarch/runner with compiled harness execution, a fixed installed captured-source read, cumulative path mandate limits, per-turn Door position delivery, SQLite replay and deferred local model responses. Context requires current and retained source, read-effect and Observation authority; source bodies use the journaled installed operation. CLI response input is limited to an unchanged regular file with a fixed 64 KiB read bound. Native declarations cannot select executable modules or grant host authority.
