changes.title: A `@mandate` that fails admission fails every mandate-gated decision closed, and admission refuses a stated `authority.moves []`
changes.summary: Breaking: 2.0.0 admitted a `@mandate` stating `authority.moves []`, and a mandate that failed admission was dropped from the admitted graph, so it silently stopped restricting: a mandate stating `moves [Bogus]` and `excluded-words [task]` let `ia preview task` run, where the same mandate with valid moves refused it (operator ruling 2026-10-12: fail closed for any `@mandate` that fails admission, reject `moves []` in the schema, the refusal names the record, `ia position` and hand edits still work). @inventarch/compliance: schema field validation, which db admission (validateGraphSchema) and the bootstrap validateSchema both run, refuses a stated empty authority.moves on a record whose word is `mandate`, when its schema declares that key as agent-system's does, with IA-COMP-FIELD-VALUE, an error at that field, each such occurrence on its own, whose message says 'authority.moves' must name at least one kernel move when stated; an absent authority.moves stays valid and restricts no move, and every other empty list stays valid (compliance C05 states this one exception). A workspace 2.0.0 admitted with `moves []` therefore has an admission error now: the machine routes keep their shapes, but over such a workspace the report route lists the finding and the read routes no longer return that mandate. @inventarch/db: every read handle and editor snapshot exposes unadmitted, with the UnadmittedRecord and UnadmittedFinding types: each record occurrence of the root view's sources that it does not admit, {identity?, word?, name?, band, path, line, endLine, finding}, for each occurrence refused names, both occurrences of an identity tie, and each record of a file refused whole by a language error or a duplicate requirement id; band is the band of the source's placement (100 authored, 90 for an adopted or installed base), and finding {code, path, line, message} the record's own admission finding from the diagnostics db already holds. A file refused whole is read from db's own parse (with the identity its compile gives, or spec 3.1's for a header the compile refused) and from its captured text, split at CRLF, CR or LF: a line opening with `@<word>` after any whitespace or Unicode format characters, which the parse did not read as a header, is listed with the name after it, wherever it stands, inside a parsed record too; on a line no parsed record spans every `@<word>` token is listed under its word; and a line that names no header is listed with no word, a record db cannot identify, when it holds one of the file's errors and no parsed record spans it (an error at a blank or `#` comment line being taken at the first line from there that is neither, so an empty or comment-only file lists nothing), when it opens with an at sign (`@`, U+FF20 or U+FE6B) after any whitespace or format characters, wherever it stands, or, in a file refused at its pragma, when it stands at column 0 and is neither blank nor a comment: a header spelled `@ mandate x`, with a full-width at sign or with a joiner after the at sign, UTF-16LE text without a byte-order mark, a stray top-level line; an error inside a parsed record's lines on a line no at sign opens stays that record's; refused, the report, the snapshot and the cache are unchanged, and nothing more is read from disk. @inventarch/runtime: the package root and ./internal/mandate-modes export refusedMandates(handle) with the RefusedMandate type, every authored (band 100) `@mandate` that failed admission, by path then line, each {identity?, path, line, code, message, unidentified?} with its own admission finding, an occurrence db lists with no word counting as a possible mandate, marked unidentified, once per line (a line db also lists a mandate at counts as that mandate), so an authored file refused whole whose records db cannot all identify fails closed, as far as db's readings reach; a mandate refused in an installed base (band 90) never counts. They also export refusedDependencies(handle), with the RefusedDependency type {dependent, field, reference, identity?, path, line, code, message}: each admitted authored `@mandate` whose authority.participant names a refused `@agent` or whose authority.scope names a refused `@workspace`, and each `@workspace` whose composition.steward names a refused `@agent`, each reference matched as authored by word and name against db's band-100 unadmitted entries, a line of a file refused whole opening `@agent <name>` or `@workspace <name>` among them; without this, a refused participant or steward `@agent` switched the default actor to another participant with looser mandates, and a refused `@workspace` left a scope-only mandate governing nowhere. A refused `@agent` or `@workspace` nothing names, a reference no authored record answers, and a record refused in an installed base keep today's reading. While either returns anything, requireMandatesAdmitted(handle, within), which governingMandates, seatedWorkspace and defaultActor call first, throws IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID marked admission 'refused' (isAdmissionRefusal(error) reads the mark), deciding workspace-wide whatever the scope token, since a refused record's scope, covers and participant cannot be trusted; through a whole-workspace token the error names the first refused mandate db identifies, else the first it cannot, as an unidentified record at path:line, possibly a `@mandate`, counting the rest by kind, else the first dependency and the record that depends on it, with the refused record's identity when known, path:line, admission code and message, and locates it as where; through a narrowed token it names no path, record or finding and carries no where. RuntimeError gains optional fourth and fifth constructor arguments, a frozen where {path, line, identity?} (the RuntimeWhere type), which that refusal and every mandateAuthorityOf refusal carry, and admission; profileRefusal and mandateRefusal keep their own empty-move-list refusal. admissionReport(root?) spells the admission report command, `ia report --root <root>` with forward slashes on win32 only when every character of the root is a letter, a digit or one of `._-/:`, else `ia report` to run from the workspace root, never a root in double quotes. evaluateMandateGuard's request takes an optional root and its decision an optional where; it branches on isAdmissionRefusal: while a record a mandate resolution reads fails admission every edit the hook selects is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE, whoever acts, naming the refused record's path:line, its finding and admissionReport(root) rather than `ia validate`, and an admitted mandate whose authority cannot be read still names its governance position. @inventarch/cli: while an authored `@mandate` fails admission, or a record an admitted mandate or workspace depends on does, `ia read`, `ia next`, `ia validate`, `ia preview`, `ia author`, `ia capture` (and `ia capture --preview`), `ia compile`, `ia project` and a workspace `ia host <host> --apply` refuse with IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID at exit 1, a where of {path, line, identity} at the first such record (identity null when unknown) and a message naming the record and its admission finding and saying a hand edit corrects it, since `ia preview` and `ia author` cannot target a record admission refused; it classifies the refusal by the runtime's mark, so a refused authored mandate sharing its identity with an admitted one of another band is no exception. The next command is the version 1 machine route `ia report`, which no mandate gates and which prints the admission report with the finding (exit 1 for a failing report, nothing on stderr): with the invocation's --root as every next command repeats it, else with the root spelled relative to the working directory (`.` or `..` segments only) when that spelling, resolved from the working directory as the route resolves --root, reaches the same real root (relative to the working directory as given first, which on win32 keeps a junction's spelling, then to its real path, so a junction or directory symlink in the path still names a root that runs), else `ia report` run from the workspace root with no path printed. An admitted mandate whose authority the runtime cannot read, such as one with a child under authority.moves, still refuses naming its governance position, now with where {path, line, identity}. `ia position`, `ia host <host> --remove --apply` (which still restores editing), `--user`, the Door and MCP reads, the install refresh, `ia-distribution`, `ia inspect` and `ia init` are unchanged and keep running. @inventarch/steward-hook: the `--hook` guard passes the registration's root to evaluateMandateGuard, so a refusal at a refused record names the admission report as admissionReport spells it; the main session's refusal still also names `ia host claude --root <root> --remove --apply --yes`; an edit the hook does not select is still not decided and managed-state protection is unchanged; a registration whose hook is not admitted, or not a declaration it can decide, is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE naming the refused record while one is refused (the hook may share its file); when the records cannot be read, the refusal names `ia validate --root <root>` if the database cannot open at all, and once it opened, the admission report while a refused mandate or dependency is among what admission refused, else `ia validate --root <root>`; a failure while the edit is decided names the admission report. @inventarch/workspace-runtime: unchanged source, but agent-profile generation's fallback for a profile that names no mandate reads governingMandates, so while a record a mandate resolution reads fails admission the rendered agent says the fallback is unavailable and names that record. Limits: the fail-closed is workspace-wide, so one broken record blocks every gated command and selected edit for every actor until its source is corrected by hand, and no in-tool repair exists; in a file refused whole, a line that declares a record with its at sign behind another character on its line (a NUL, a letter, other text) is not seen when it stands inside the lines of a record the parse reads, or indented in a file refused at its pragma, since no reading names it and an error there is that record's (db D15 states the readings exactly), while any line outside such a record that only mentions `@mandate`, any line an at sign opens that names no header, any error line outside a parsed record that names no header, and any top-level line of a file refused at its pragma that is neither blank nor a comment, is read as a possible mandate, failing closed; a mandate in a file db never reads (an extension other than lowercase `.ia`, or a path under node_modules, dist or .git) restricts nothing and is reported nowhere, as in 2.0.0; a --root the invocation gave is repeated as given, as every next command repeats it; position, body(K), the packet renderer and the Door operations render no mandate for a refused record and never refuse; the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and every `ia scope` form keep their shapes.

changes.title: The runtime resolves the `@mandate` records that govern an actor, its default actor and a mode's refusal profile
changes.summary: @inventarch/runtime exports governingMandates(handle, within, {actor?, path?, workspace?}), defaultActor(handle, within, workspace) and profileRefusal(mandates, mode, words?) from the package root and the @inventarch/runtime/internal/mandate-modes subpath, with the GoverningOptions, GoverningMandate, DefaultActor, ProfileMandate and ProfileVerdict types, and registers IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR in RUNTIME_CODES and MANDATE_CODES. governingMandates and defaultActor read through the scope token alone, profileRefusal reads nothing, and none needs a clean workspace: one with admission errors resolves what admission admitted, except that while an authored `@mandate` fails admission, or a record an admitted mandate or workspace depends on does, governingMandates and defaultActor fail closed with IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID (described in the mandate-admission note). A record at runtime placement is never read, only authored (band 100) `@mandate` records govern, and only those of the workspace's closure as position reads it (without a workspace, that of the workspace position seats the path in, else the repository's own), so a mandate under another workspace's declared root never governs or names a participant there. governingMandates returns the governing mandates by identity, each with its moves, covers and excluded words (present when the record states the key) and its participant and scope references resolved to identities: with workspace or path, those whose authority.scope names the workspace or whose authority.covers selects the path, either sufficing, and one that states neither key with a value (a declared empty list locates nothing, so it never lifts a restriction) wherever its participant acts (with actor, only when that participant is the actor); with neither, every one. An actor drops no governing mandate: each then carries binds, true when its participant is that `@agent` or it names none. defaultActor names the `@agent` a mandate-gated command acts as: the workspace's composition.steward when it is an authored (band 100) `@agent` (an installed steward names none, as if none were stated), else the one authored participant its scoped mandates name, and lists in actors the identities a command may be told to act as, the participants and the authored steward; with several participants and no authored steward it names none and returns IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR, whose next command is ia position --seat <workspace> --shape governance, and with none it returns only a reason. profileRefusal returns {refusal?, notice?}: it leaves out a mandate that binds another participant and returns IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR when every governing mandate does, or when the rest bind several participants, whose moves it never pools; otherwise a mode is allowed when any remaining mandate grants its move (lists it or declares no moves), else IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-MOVE, and, when words are given, a word any of them excludes is IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-WORD; each refusal names ia position --seat <mandate> --shape governance; with no governing mandate nothing is restricted and the notice says so. A missing token, an actor or workspace that is not an admitted record of its word, an unknown mode, or a governing mandate whose authority mandateAuthorityOf refuses is IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID. Limits: @inventarch/cli's mandate profile (its gated commands, defaultActor included) and the edit guard (evaluateMandateGuard, which @inventarch/steward-hook's `--hook` mode calls for each edit an authored `@hook` selects) consult them, and @inventarch/workspace-runtime's agent-profile generation reads governingMandates for a profile that names no mandate; no Door operation does; mandateRefusal still names ia inspect <mandate> --edges both; a mandate grants no host permission; the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2, every ia scope form, position, body(K) and the packet renderer are unchanged.

changes.title: Align native archives once and enforce independent content versions
changes.summary: The bundled public language and system archives move once to native 2.1.0. The current composition fixture tracks that selected native base while retaining exact equality with the initialized starter. Future native releases retain unchanged archive versions, require individual change notes, and refuse changed bytes under an already published native identity and version. Native selection remains independent of the coordinated npm release version.

changes.title: Separate public vocabulary payloads from repository work and release controls
changes.summary: Public native packages retain their vocabulary, implementations and teaching assets while repository work and neutral examples use separate authored and fixture corpora. Exact root release controls preserve installed distribution identities without coupling every vocabulary package; archives using this source profile require an updated consumer, while previous archives and engine locks remain supported. Qualification compares the actual packed dependency cycle groups with the maintained policy. Workspace composition accepts system references only; repository qualification rejects copied active npm versions and package counts while retaining version-pinned historical decisions.

changes.title: Repair public contract citations
changes.summary: Implementation and qualification comments now cite maintained public contract sections, and registry documentation links the collection and adoption contract. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

changes.title: Align public qualification documentation
changes.summary: Public SDK qualification documents its committed source seal, retained archive receipt and manifest-derived package membership. Maintained tooling contracts and host test comments now describe the public repository without obsolete source-export requirements. Runtime behavior and active assertions are unchanged. Qualification tools initialize the physical temporary directory before importing shared selectors.

changes.title: Maintain public implementation and release contracts
changes.summary: Package source citations now resolve to maintained public specifications. Release preparation uses a public repository input seal and reviewed package membership, with independent native and npm versions; local qualification does not establish registry publication or host activation.

changes.title: Qualify separated workspace and public examples
changes.summary: CLI and workspace-runtime regressions now test repository maintenance records separately from explicit public examples, preserving exact admission, refusal, binding and generated-file checks. Starter fixtures and engine assertions track the current distribution engine.

changes.title: Install registry kits and adopt pinned source workspaces
changes.summary:
Registry consumers can now read release, kit and workspace indexes through the same bounded provider interface, with the existing Inventarch default and release-index API retained. `ia install <kit>` resolves its distribution members through archive integrity and admission checks, refreshes registered packet projections, and locks the resulting exact distribution closure for offline restore. `ia init --adopt <workspace>` and the new preview-first `ia adopt <workspace>` pin source bytes, update the workspace source declaration, capture the result and refresh registered projections; a failed capture or projection reports the applied adoption and one version-pinned retry command retaining the root and explicit registry; `ia doctor` reports mount pins and placement. Public registry schemas are also available from @inventarch/service-contracts.

Adopted registry sources enter at open band 50, below installed/adopted band 90 and authored band 100. Existing version-1 adopted bindings remain supported, and captured reads preserve the open source identity and revision. Workspace indexes accept bounded native sources and text documentation; they refuse executable/configuration paths, remote credentials and authority records such as `@mandate`, `@agent-profile`, `@execution-binding`, `@hook`, `@capability` and `@check`. Adoption does not grant execution authority. Changed inputs, unlisted destination entries, modified source bytes, source paths excluded from physical capture and replacement pins refuse; destination membership and the physical native revision are rechecked before publication without deleting owner data; an ordinary binding-publication failure restores this operation's authored declaration. Rollback removes the exact open binding and matching source declaration, then captures and reprojects; keep immutable trees needed by retained captures. Process-crash recovery remains manual: inspect the declaration and binding before removing a stale adoption lock.

The optional-distribution packer now accepts a selected directory, owned systems, descriptor and explicit assets, and can prepare kit metadata. The existing product-structure wrapper keeps identical archive bytes for the same inputs. These operations prepare local artifacts; publishing release indexes or packages remains a separate action.

changes.title: Recognize repository native records and release roots
changes.summary: Repository ownership now assigns native records and release controls outside reusable system folders to the root contract. Qualification fixtures follow the separated live workspace, public examples, current distribution engine and production dependency partitions without weakening admission or cycle checks.

changes.title: Validate retained root release controls consistently
changes.summary: Expanded and retained installations now enforce the same exact root release-control declaration and system roots as archive verification, including when all content and metadata pins have been recomputed. Existing system-source admission and legacy installations remain unchanged.

changes.title: Admit bounded runner journal claims as optional runtime evidence
changes.summary: @inventarch/db adds writeRunnerEvidence and the RunnerEvidenceWrite type, RUNNER_EVIDENCE_FORMAT, RUNNER_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY and InputSnapshot.runnerEvidence. Readers opened with evidence:true can admit fixed-field `@run` and `@observation` projections from current-revision, source-bound local runner journal receipts. Observations reference their run; run status and phase recorded identify a journal projection rather than live engine state. The writer checks bounded plain data, hashes and monotonic journal prefixes, then stages and atomically replaces one receipt under an exclusive lock. Readers reject malformed, stale, colliding, linked, oversized or source-mismatched receipts. Evidence changes the reader revision without changing authoredRevision or existing authored admission. Validation evidence retains its independent exact reproduction gate. Journal integrity is not external attestation, execution authorization or proof of real-world effects; session replay remains the runner's responsibility. No release version or publication is selected by this additive change.

changes.title: Recognize linked runner entry points
changes.summary: The runner uses the shared entry-point helper so invoking its executable through a link starts the CLI. Importing its main module remains inert; runtime execution logic is unchanged.

changes.title: `ia validate` admits a `@check` that names an evaluator that is not built in, to bind it; every other reader but `ia preview` and `ia author` keeps strict admission
changes.summary: Relaxed, structural check admission (plan amendments C15 and C21), used by the validate request and, as their own note says, by ia preview and ia author, which 2.0.0 did not have. Released behavior is that a `@check` whose check.implementation or check.runs names an id that is not a built-in evaluator is refused with IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN and is not admitted. That stays the default for every reader of the admitted graph: the nine machine routes (scope, context, select, get, records, resolve, search, traverse, report), every ia scope form, ia position, ia next, ia read, ia capture, ia host, ia project, ia doctor, the MCP door, ia-distribution's other commands, and db open, the Door and compliance evaluate called without the new option; a test answers the nine routes and ia scope over an unknown-runner fixture byte for byte as strict admission does. What changed: ia validate and ia-distribution validate now admit structurally, so such a check is admitted, reported in the Checks section and bound (unavailable when no host catalog lists the evaluator), and in the same workspace that ia validate reports as admitted every strict reader counts such a check as an IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN error (ia host and ia project refuse the workspace with IA-CLI-CONFLICT, and ia capture records the error in its snapshot and exits 1), which ia validate's summary states, naming each such check; a check naming two different evaluators (IA-COMP-CHECK-CONFLICT) or none (IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN) is still refused by both. @inventarch/compliance adds validateCheckStructure(node) and ReportOptions.checks ('strict', the default, or 'structural'); @inventarch/db adds OpenOptions.checks and ViewOptions.checks with the same values and the same default (a handle opened structural never uses the cache, and its preview drafts structurally too), and @inventarch/runtime's DoorOptions, which extends OpenOptions, therefore accepts them, while the Door the machine routes open stays strict; @inventarch/distribution adds SessionOptions.checks. Not compatible with 2.0.0 for a consumer that relied on ia validate or ia-distribution validate refusing an unknown evaluator: such a workspace now validates with exit 0 when nothing else is wrong.
